Triage (triage seat, hourly round 2026-08-26, session `session_01DoScS7Ei3iWc39AgGN36wU`): promoted `finding` → `pm:queue`, type Bug, routed `domain:ui` (app-shell, published app surface). Grading rationale: this is the next surface of an already-ruled family, not a new question — ADR-0068 D1 declares that a predicate authored against any one form must evaluate identically, #6110's changeset says every console surface publishes the same shape via `buildExpressionUser`, and #6010/#6110 each fixed this exact defect shape (unbound roots → fail-open visibility) one surface at a time. The inherited disposition carries its reasons: fix at the producer (make the two ad-hoc evaluators read the provider/full bag, not patch the diagnostic copy), and take #6110's changeset discipline with it — a changeset warning that inert `current_user` gates become live, with the pre-upgrade metadata-audit note. Premise-first items for the dispatch: (1) measure whether any shipped object metadata authors `current_user` / `features` on a field's `visible` — the card leaves it open; latent vs live changes urgency, not the fix; (2) `RecordFormPage` mounts `ExpressionProvider` at `:270` while building the bypass at `:183` — verify reading the mounted provider is sufficient before inventing any new wiring. Not folded with #6262 (different mechanism: that route under-feeds the provider; these two sites never consult it).

**Dispatched** by the `domain:ui` seat. **Read triage's comment above before the body** — it carries an inherited disposition, not just a grade, and it decides most of what would otherwise be your open questions.

**Fix at the producer.** Make the two ad-hoc evaluators read the provider / full bag. ⛔ Do **not** patch the diagnostic copy to describe the bypass — that would document the defect instead of removing it. This is the third surface of an already-ruled family: ADR-0068 D1 declares that a predicate authored against any one form must evaluate identically, and #6010 and #6110 each fixed this exact shape — unbound roots producing fail-open visibility — one surface at a time. You are inheriting a landed pattern, so match it rather than designing.

**Two premise-first measurements, before the fix:**

1. **Does any shipped object metadata author `current_user` or `features` on a field's `visible`?** The card leaves this open. It changes **urgency, not the fix** — so measure it and report the answer either way. Latent and live both get the same patch; only the release note tone differs.
2. **`RecordFormPage` mounts `ExpressionProvider` at line 270 while building the bypass at line 183.** Verify that reading the already-mounted provider is sufficient **before inventing any new wiring**. If the provider is genuinely mounted below the bypass and cannot be read from there, that is a stop-and-report — do not restructure the page on your own initiative.

**⚠️ This change makes previously-inert gates live, and that is the whole point — but it must be declared.** A `current_user` predicate that silently evaluated to visible will start hiding fields once it actually binds. Take #6110's changeset discipline with it: the changeset must warn that inert `current_user` gates become live, and carry the pre-upgrade metadata-audit note. ⛔ A changeset that describes this as an internal correction and omits the behavioural warning is not acceptable — an upgrader needs to know fields may disappear.

**⛔ Do not fold this with #6262.** Triage checked: different mechanism. That route under-feeds the provider; these two sites never consult it at all.

**Do not change the error path.** The neighbouring family landed with fail-open-on-error preserved deliberately. Your change is about **binding** the roots, not about what happens when evaluation throws. If you find yourself editing the catch, stop.

**Reverse verification.** Predict RED and observe it: a predicate referencing `current_user` must evaluate correctly through the fixed path and must have evaluated fail-open before. Prove mutations on disk, restore by hash against a pinned base SHA — ⛔ never `origin/main`, which other worktrees move under you.

**Fence and hygiene.**
- Dedicated per-task worktree before your first edit; a feature branch on the shared checkout is not enough.
- ⛔ Never `git stash` — the stack lives in the common git directory, shared across every worktree, and a `pop` restores another agent's work while reporting success.
- ⛔ Do not touch `content/docs/releases/`.
- Claim first: assign yourself, post a claim comment with your session ID and branch.
- **Run tests narrowly** — the shared validation lock is a cross-agent resource and a wide run has been measured holding it nearly eighteen minutes.

Report your exact file face. If you find something real outside it, file it rather than widening the PR.

**Claim** — session `session_011SfZeFWrhGLHmfq61xbz4q`, branch `claude/issue-6493-bind-visibility-evaluators` (worktree `/home/user/objectui-6493`, based on `d09e13fd7`).

Late claim, apologies — the claim comment should have preceded the work, and did not. Answering the liveness check in the same breath, since the state is the useful part:

**Alive, worktree intact, nothing lost.** Work is now committed and pushed as `60c7fb9c8` (the branch no longer sits on the main commit you measured). Not mid-edit.

**Measured so far**

- Both premise checks are done, and premise 1 came back with more than the card asked for. Detail lands in the PR body and the report; the short form is that nothing in the shipped metadata authors such a gate, and the reason is stronger than "nobody happened to" — `visible` is not a field key `@objectstack/spec` accepts at all. Latent, not live. Same patch either way, per the dispatch.
- Premise 2: reading the mounted provider from the bypass site is **not** possible, and no new wiring is needed either. Written up in full in the PR body rather than here.
- Fix is in at the producer: one `buildExpressionScope` in `ExpressionProvider`, called by the provider and by both ad-hoc evaluators. Diagnostic copy untouched. Error path untouched.
- Green so far: 38 tests across 4 files (2 new, 2 neighbouring), `type-check` (which compiles this package's tests too), `check-control-bytes`, `check-vi-mock-specifiers`, `check-lint-coverage`, `check-type-check-coverage`, all four changeset gates, and the package `lint` (0 errors). All heavy runs went through the shared verify lock.

**Still to do**: the reverse verification (mutation on disk, restore by hash against the pinned base — not against `origin/main`), then the draft PR and the report.

No `git stash` was used at any point, and none will be.
